access.edition_or_version: First edition: London, Victor Gollancz in association with Smythe, 1987 (12 November 1987 per bibliographic records verified earlier in this session; SFE entry corroborates London: Victor Gollancz, 1987)

mechanics.premise: Death — the cosmic office most sacred and feared — takes an apprentice and is revealed as a well-meaning, overworked civil servant who struggles with humanity.
mechanics.deflation_targets: The most solemn register of all (mortality itself) domesticated: personified Death is given a household, a job description, and uncomprehending social curiosity, so awe collapses into bureaucracy and small talk.
mechanics.licensed_frame: The established comic-fantasy conventions of the Discworld series (corroborated via the SFE Pratchett entry) license treating the sacred office as a character among others.
mechanics.point_of_view: Omniscient narrator with wide ironic latitude, free to slide between an apprentice's bewilderment and Death's literal-mindedness.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Straight-faced personification; solemn abstraction answered with concrete domestic detail; the deflation carried by narration's calm rather than by anyone mocking aloud.
mechanics.dialogue: Death's uncomprehending literalness turns ceremonial speech into comedy without a single character being derided.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Awe -> amusement at familiarity -> genuine pathos when the deflated office proves capable of caring — the tone yields to feeling at the stakes peak.
mechanics.boundaries_and_restraint: Irreverence aimed at an office/abstraction, never at bereaved people in-scene — a model for the punching-up/no-real-victims boundary; critical context via src-irreverent-butler-guilty-2001 (bibliographic only).
mechanics.conventions: Anchors the Discworld device of running cosmic offices as comic workplaces.
mechanics.innovation_or_subversion: Makes death — the paradigm sacred subject — safe for affectionate deflation while preserving its weight.
mechanics.critical_reception: Established Pratchett's comic reputation beyond parody; scholarly context collection Guilty of Literature (2001) treats him as a critic's subject (record bibliographic only).
mechanics.audience_reception: Among the most-remembered Discworld novels; Death became the series' beloved figure — evidence that licensed deflation can increase, not diminish, affection for the sacred subject.
